metadata.title: Minnesota surveillance and enforcement coverage
metadata.license: Headlines, outlet names and links only. No article text is copied, mirrored or stored. Each link resolves to the publisher, who holds the copyright.

coverage: This is press coverage, not a record of what happened. A contract signed with no reporter in the room does not appear here.
Google News decides what its index returns and caps each search at about 100 results, so a busy month is a sample rather than a complete list.
Stories about individual people are removed before anything is saved — including stories about arrests, court cases, and named officers. Only coverage of the systems themselves is kept.
Coverage skews toward outlets Google indexes well. Small-market radio and weekly papers are under-represented relative to how much of this reporting they actually do.
knownGaps: Hmong-language and Spanish-language Minnesota outlets are not indexed as sources by Google News, so this feed structurally cannot see their reporting — the communities carrying most of this enforcement are covered here only when an English-language outlet also files the story. Adding those outlets to the source list would not fix it; the upstream has no items to return.

Every link here points at Google News rather than at the newspaper, because Google no longer publishes the article address and the only way to obtain it would break this project's own rule against scraping private interfaces. Links resolve today; they are outside our control and may not resolve in a few years. The outlet, headline and date beside each link are the durable citation — a story can be found from those even when the link dies.
